title: Check yourself: Path-scoped rules, file size and the practice

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Testing conventions must govern spec files that live in dozens of different folders, and no other file. What delivers that?

options.text: A scoped rule whose glob matches by extension anywhere
options.says: One glob follows the type across folders, and the rule loads when a matching file is read or edited.

options.text: A separate memory file placed in every one of those folders
options.says: Ruled out because the guide's reason for the glob is "test files spread throughout a codebase", and a copy in each folder would have to be kept in step.

options.text: An import of the conventions from the project root file
options.says: Ruled out because an import "moves text to another file and loads it at launch", so the conventions would reach every task.

options.text: A section for each project in the personal memory file
options.says: Ruled out because personal rules "apply to every project on your machine", so they neither scope to test files nor reach the team.

origin.section: Path-scoped rules, file size and the practice

questions.stem: A rule meant for infrastructure code loads in every session instead. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The rules folder sits below the working directory
options.says: Ruled out because "Every Markdown file under .claude/rules/ is a rule", wherever the session starts.

options.text: Infrastructure files are always opened at the start of a session
options.says: Ruled out because a scoped rule loads when Claude uses Read, Write or Edit on a matching file, "not on every tool use".

options.text: Its frontmatter is invalid YAML, so the scoping is dropped
options.says: When the frontmatter does not parse, the rule is treated as unscoped.

options.text: The rule's file name does not match the folder it governs
options.says: Ruled out because the file name plays no part, since `paths` "is the only field Claude Code reads in a rule".

origin.section: Rules that load on a match
